name: Sparring Match

angles.text: As a warrior, you know Tang Stonehoof's sparring ring teaches more than one discipline. He believes combat fundamentals, courage, and resolve help every adventurer.

As a tauren, you may hear Tang Stonehoof use traditional turns of phrase such as “sharpen their horns” when speaking of testing one's mettle. He welcomes any willing adversary to the sparring arena, whatever their origins.

faq.answer: Tang Stonehoof oversees the local sparring arena as its combat instructor. He teaches those who follow paths beyond the warrior's and invites promising adventurers to face novices or willing peers.

Tang Stonehoof asks you to defeat three opponents in the arena. They may be willing adventurers who duel you or Novice Warriors training under his guidance. The trial tests your readiness and skill in direct combat.
faq.q: What does Tang Stonehoof require for the sparring match?

faq.answer: Tang Stonehoof believes direct combat benefits every adventurer, whether they wield a blade, bow, or magic. In his arena, lineage and class discipline matter less than the will to test yourself and strengthen your resolve.
faq.q: Why does a warrior instructor train other classes?

faq.answer: The contest takes place in the open sparring arena before Tang Stonehoof. Novice combatants train there, and willing challengers can face one another on equal footing.
faq.q: Where does the sparring match take place?

faq.answer: Yes. Tang Stonehoof accepts victories over Novice Warriors training in the arena or other adventurers defeated in formal duels. He asks only that you test your abilities against willing opponents.
faq.q: Can you duel other players instead of the novice warriors?

faq.answer: After you prove yourself against three adversaries, Tang acknowledges your skill and places his hope in the new generation. He offers medical supplies for your wounds before the harsh road ahead.
faq.q: What does Tang Stonehoof say when you complete the match?

sections.body: Tang Stonehoof welcomes travelers of every path into his sparring ring. He takes special notice of those who follow a tradition beyond the warrior's, yet believes martial discipline and direct combat teach lessons to all who travel through a dangerous world.
sections.title: The Sparring Grounds

sections.body: In Tang Stonehoof's arena, lineage and weapon matter little. You may wield a sword, bow, or magic, but you must defeat three willing opponents. They may be Novice Warriors in training or fellow adventurers who agree to duel. Victory earns Tang's respect and bandages for wounds suffered in honest combat.
sections.title: Sharpening the Horns

summary: At Tang Stonehoof's arena, newcomers face a trial of strength. Whatever their class or background, they can meet three novices or willing duelists and show their skill in combat.
